The most important distinction is whether you're scanning parts to reproduce their shape or to manufacture replacement components with tight tolerances.

What matters most

For mechanical reverse engineering, prioritize:

Volumetric accuracy: How measurement error behaves across the entire part, not just at a single point.

Blue laser scanning: Especially useful for metallic, dark, or reflective surfaces.

Scan-to-CAD workflow: Mesh capture alone doesn't automatically produce an editable STEP or parametric CAD model.

Small-feature performance: Holes, slots, sharp edges, and mating surfaces can be more challenging than broad curved surfaces.

For precision mating surfaces, supplement optical scanning with calipers, micrometers, or a CMM.
